clue.text: The academic world quietly skewers French philosopher

indicators.note: to skewer is to run something through, so one piece pierces the middle of the other

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French existentialist writer and philosopher
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A scholar's soft-spoken but cutting attack on a famous French thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus was a French writer usually filed as an existentialist philosopher; the musical sign for quiet is pierced into his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university, so it stands by extension for academic life in general.

clue.text: Country originally banned alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: the original, i.e. first, letter of the word is banned, so it is removed

parts.note: Wales is a country of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A nation that once imposed prohibition on liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the W from WALES leaves ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, a kind of drink containing alcohol.

clue.text: Theatre providing entertainment for children?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a building where plays are staged
second meaning: a toy house that children play in

explanation.surface: A theatre that puts on shows aimed at young audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, playful sense: a small model house children use for games, often called a Wendy house in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a building for staging drama and a miniature house built for children's games.

clue.text: He guards small gate, perhaps

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a gate is one example of a way in

explanation.surface: A man stands watch over a little gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that gate is just one example of the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, so 'he guards' describes his job.

clue.text: Find out about alternative careers and then start to hesitate

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of the next word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of hesitate

explanation.surface: Advice to someone weighing a change of job: look into other options, then pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To research a subject is to investigate it and find out facts about it.

clue.text: Bully kills strumpet, popular and impish creature

indicators.note: to bully is to push around, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
something popular is said to be in

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid headline about a thug who murders a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of KILLS, STRUMPET and IN are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the mischievous little man in the Grimm fairy tale who spins straw into gold.

clue.text: Flattery finally gets you — and us — in a lather

parts.note: soap, as in soft soap, is informal for flattery

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: the final letter of each of gets, you, and, us

explanation.surface: Smooth talk gets everyone worked up into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in a lather' means flustered; here the phrase splits, and 'lather' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapsuds are the foam formed when soap is mixed with water, which is what lather is.

clue.text: Soothsayer and a swami putting foot over head

indicators.note: the foot is the bottom letter of a down entry, and it is moved up above the top one

parts.note: taken as written
a swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a guru

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller and a holy man doing a yoga pose with a leg behind the head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the foot is the last letter and the head the first, so the final letter of the teacher's title moves to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman priest who foretold events, so the word means a prophet or soothsayer.

clue.text: Imagining making a baby

definitions.meaning: first meaning: forming an idea in the mind

explanation.surface: Someone daydreaming about starting a family.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceive is both to form a mental picture of something and to become pregnant with a child.

clue.text: Quiet time with a partner starts to nark us more each year

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an era is a period of time, with A as the word written
in bridge, North is South's partner, abbreviated N

indicators.note: the starts of the following words means each one contributes just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of nark, us, more

explanation.surface: A couple's quiet moments together get more annoying every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is used up by the initials, so nothing joins the definition; in bridge, North and South are partners. To nark is British slang for to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for yearly, used in finance for rates charged or paid every year.

clue.text: It causes sudden pain as woman embraces Joe

indicators.note: one who embraces wraps their arms round another, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a woman's name
GI Joe is slang for an American soldier, so Joe can mean GI

explanation.surface: Heartache strikes when a woman hugs Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is a condition of sudden chest pain caused by too little blood reaching the heart.

clue.text: Drastically restyle her at address in W1

indicators.note: a drastic change is a radical one, so the letters are thoroughly reworked

parts.note: taken as written, all twelve letters

explanation.surface: A hairdresser in a smart London postcode gives a client a radical makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is the postcode for London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Harley Street is a street in London's W1 district famous for private doctors' practices.

clue.text: Each monk is embarrassed to have a dirty habit

indicators.note: someone embarrassed is flustered and thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, all ten letters

explanation.surface: Every monk is ashamed of a grubby habit, with a nod to the monk's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' reads as part of the verb but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain-smoke is to light one cigarette after another, a dirty habit in both senses.

clue.text: Lighthouse protecting you in the old days

indicators.note: something protecting another keeps it safely inside, so the word sits within the one before

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A lighthouse that kept you safe long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic singular form of the pronoun you.

clue.text: Almost understand case for drug

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to see is to understand
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A lawyer nearly grasps the argument for a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a legal argument or a container, but it is the grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming drug that induces sleep or relaxation.

clue.text: It's hard to negotiate with drunk guy, perhaps

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a guy is a rope holding a tent steady, one kind of rope

explanation.surface: Bargaining with someone who has had too much is tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate' reads as bargaining but means getting across.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a high wire that acrobats must cross with great difficulty, hard to negotiate in the sense of traverse.

clue.text: Woman taking part in battles showing caution

indicators.note: to take part in something is to be inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: wars are battles
Ines is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman joining combat carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness is the state of being careful about danger, a synonym of caution.

clue.text: Burning novel? Irate men of letters!

parts.note: a fire that is lit is burning

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Furious critics want to set a book on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being burnt; it is an adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the educated, literary class, writers and scholars in general.

clue.text: Information and energy combine to form hereditary unit

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A science lesson on how data and energy produce something inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is the basic unit of heredity passed from parent to offspring.

clue.text: Mammals with just over 100 people who look after them

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals, just over C
vets are the people who care for animals

explanation.surface: A herd of animals with about a hundred keepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Civets are small catlike carnivorous mammals of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Doctor using typist's chair

indicators.note: the letters are being used to make something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A GP short of furniture borrows a secretary's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is often an anagram indicator, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor specialising in mental illness.

clue.text: Whack 150, get dismissed

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer hits a big score and then loses their wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter scores runs until dismissed, or out.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow, so it means a whack.

clue.text: 24 type of vegetable

parts.note: the answer to 24 across read as an instruction: the word keel, turned over

explanation.surface: A cross-reference presented as a botanical category: one answer names a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is KEEL OVER, which read as an instruction says turn KEEL over.
explanation.definitionFit: A leek is an onion-family vegetable with a long white stem.

clue.text: Shy, evenly mottled prairie wolf

parts.note: coy means bashful or shy

indicators.note: evenly means the even-numbered positions, so only the second, fourth and sixth letters are kept

parts.note: letters two, four and six of mottled

explanation.surface: A timid wild dog with a uniformly patchy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evenly mottled' looks like a description of fur; it picks out letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a small North American wild dog of the plains, also called the prairie wolf.

clue.text: Faint expression of fear about partner

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright
a lover is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A weak squeal of alarm about one's other half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faint' reads as an adjective for the squeal, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse suddenly, as someone does when they faint.

clue.text: To throw something from ship or plane is not unusual

definitions.text: To throw something from ship or plane

parts.note: a jet is a kind of aeroplane

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that dumping cargo from vessels or aircraft is a common thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' does double duty: it ends the definition and starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard cargo or equipment from a ship or aircraft, often to lighten it.

clue.text: Slippery eel's head found in Serpentine

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so one letter sits within the other word

parts.note: serpentine means snakelike, which is snaky

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top or opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of eel

explanation.surface: An eel is spotted in the Serpentine, the lake in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Serpentine look like the Hyde Park lake; it is the adjective meaning snakelike.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery can describe a sly, untrustworthy person, which is what sneaky means.
